column4: Game creator detail is descriptive content but unknown security is not affirmative unrestricted access.
Genre detail has no explicit public-access statement or caller authorization evidence.
Attachment relatedId and relatedType are opaque relations; secret-key or JWT authentication does not establish ownership.
Bank account customerId is an inferred relation without a verified caller-customer lookup or owner-only rule.
Creating a blocklist uses authentication alternatives but no specified caller role or object-owner policy.
Credential customerId and username identify data subjects without verified authorization mapping to the caller.
Service instance retrieval uses UserSecurity but supplies no owner or tenant authorization relationship.
Offering service-instance list has authentication but only pagination wrappers, not a verified object access rule.
System inventory detail requires RhIdentity without a supplied caller organization or owner binding.
Sale-listing metadata requires a security scheme and does not explicitly guarantee unrestricted API access.
My selling-order shipment suggests seller access but shipping-only fields cannot support a verified order-owner lookup.
Certificate export has Basic or bearer authentication and no concrete caller role or ownership evidence.
Campaign event detail requires an API token and only result wrappers are available to infer authorization.
Accepting a change request has no explicit approver role or owner relationship in the supplied result fields.
Account-key created_by and organization_id are competing inferred authorization hints without verified lookup semantics.
Organization update has inferred id and client_id but no verified caller-tenant relation.
Scan template ACL, creator and organization fields imply multiple possible access paths without a verified policy binding.
User client_admin and org_roles are response attributes, not proof of an administrator requirement or self-access lookup.
Sending a user's reset email uses bearer authentication but role fields do not establish caller authorization.
Deletion organizationId is inferred response metadata without a verified tenant identity or lookup mapping.
CRM account owner and creator describe sales assignments, not a verified API caller authorization relationship.
Call instructions have unknown security and no owner or tenant lookup fields.
Call user is activity metadata and user_guid filtering does not establish owner-only access.
Email user and recipient fields describe participants without a verified authorized caller relationship.
Shipping batch retrieval requires an API key but lacks any supplied batch ownership relation.
Carrier settings are account configuration without a verified caller-account authorization mapping.
Inline-script account_id is inferred; read_inline_script_tags scope does not establish personal or tenant ownership.
Render owner and plan are response-derived fields, not a verified owner lookup or required membership tier.
Audio-license listing uses licenses.view permission and team-history filters without a specific owner or membership policy.
Alert report includes userId and teamId without a verified choice of individual versus team authorization.
Alert annotation userId describes annotation authorship, not a verified alert-owner access rule.
Notification userId identifies a recipient without proving that only that user may retrieve the alert notifications.
Reopening an alert has inferred teamId and lifecycle metadata but no verified tenant authorization lookup.
admin.conversations:read is a permission scope rather than proof of a required app role; channel-to-enterprise binding is absent.
CompanyAdministrator and CompanyMonitor occur as scopes with a Pin alternative, not verified application roles or tenant lookup evidence.
CompanyMonitor scope and Pin authentication do not establish a verified user-self or company authorization rule for check-in.
Emergency reporting has company/user context but no verified caller identity mapping; scope names alone are not roles.
Ending monitoring uses authentication alternatives without a verified user ownership or company-tenant binding.
Location reporting identifies company and user but inferred company data does not verify authorization lookup semantics.
Device configuration includes sensitive keys but no supplied owner binding or concrete caller authorization policy.
Group audit filter projectId and userId are query-like metadata rather than verified tenant or owner lookup evidence.
Group-tag deletion has unknown security and no verified group access relationship.
Adding an organization integration provides credential configuration without a verified tenant or caller-role policy.
Import target owner identifies a source repository owner rather than the API caller's authorization subject.
Organization integration-setting update has no verified organization binding or concrete caller role.
Authenticated-user following retrieval concerns a relationship to another user, not ownership of that target user's profile.
My-track retrieval has user and sharing fields but no verified flattened ownership lookup.
Playlist-track access uses authentication and sharing metadata without a verified playlist authorization relationship.
Comment user_id denotes authorship while ClientId authentication does not imply owner-only or unrestricted read access.
Accepting my contract uses AgentToken but agent/contract wrappers do not provide a verified ownership lookup.
